content.text:
`/electron/init-oauth-proxy` now returns each cookie from the inner sign-in as its own `Set-Cookie` header, in the order the inner response emitted them.

I ran the Electron test file and it passes (85 tests, including the new one). `tsc --noEmit` on the package is clean. I didn't run `pnpm typecheck` repo-wide.

The change is in `packages/electron/src/routes.ts`. The old code read the inner response with `headers.get("set-cookie")`, which merges everything into one comma-joined string. It now reads `getSetCookie()` and appends each cookie to the response headers separately, so attributes pass through untouched. I didn't touch the redirect handling, so a redirect URL with `redirect: true` still gives a `302` with a `Location` header. If the inner response sets no cookies, no `Set-Cookie` header is added.

I added one test to `packages/electron/test/electron.test.ts`. It mocks the global `fetch` to return two cookies and checks that `asResponse: true` gives back exactly two headers, starting with `first.cookie=one` and `second.cookie=two`. It doesn't check attribute preservation, the redirect case or the no-cookie case; the existing tests passed, and I didn't check what they cover for those.

I didn't commit anything.
